title: Strokes you can type
goal: Which right-pinky chords cannot be pressed, and how a word that needed one is swapped or split.

blocks.x: Some chords cannot be pressed; the generator never writes one. The right pinky has four keys in a 2x2 block:

A stroke needing a diagonal pair or exactly three of the four keys is not a stroke: a physical limit of the hand, so a hard filter, not a cost. The left hand and other fingers are unlimited (the left pinky has one key, `S-`).
What happens to a word that needed one

An untypable stroke is dropped or repaired before it competes. Candidates (gold briefs, the rules' reading, spelling variants, ladder steps, short forms, `-S` respellings) get two kinds of repair; the solver picks by cost. **A free one-stroke form always beats a split.**

One or two pinky keys are swapped for their voiced or unvoiced partner ([[-T]]/[[-D]], [[-S]]/[[-Z]]) when the result is typable. [[-TZ]] becomes [[-TS]] or [[-DZ]]; [[-SD]] becomes `-ZD` or `-ST`. These cost what the original did (same key count); a swapped stroke held by a more common word loses it, like any collision.

If no swap is free, the pinky keys stay in order while they can be pressed together; the rest moves to a joined continuation stroke. [[-SD]] becomes [[-S]] then [[+-D]]; [[-TDZ]] becomes [[-TD]] then [[+-Z]].
Only a word whose outline has exactly one untypable stroke gets swaps. A word with more than one is split.

head: Kind of outline
What happens
rows: Backups, family members, phrases and alternates
An untypable result is not offered. A phrase whose OR'd strokes would make a diagonal does not exist.
Refused: `!build` stops with an error naming the word.
Ignores a plain reading that is untypable.

blocks.x: Four rare words have no outline because their only repair fails the consonant check on the voiced `-D`: *cleansed*, *pulsed*, *blitzed*, *repulsed*. They are still typable from their syllables, e.g. [[cleansed|-BLG/+EFPBD]], and [the solver](#/ref/fallback) reads a run of their sounds as the word.
